data.title: Melittin attenuates imiquimod-induced psoriatic dermatitis in mice: a role for autophagy activation via PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway suppression.
data.authors: Hafez SA; Ahmed AA; Elkhoely A; Ahmed AAE

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Melittin (bee venom, 80 mg/kg i.p.) reduces psoriatic dermatitis severity by 60% in an imiquimod mouse model by suppressing PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling and activating autophagy.
data.abstract_excerpt: Melittin, the main component in bee venom, exhibits valuable anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties in various diseases; meanwhile, its effect on psoriasis has not been explored yet. Mice were divided into 5 groups: Control, Imiquimod (IMQ), methotrexate (MTX, 1 mg/kg), melittin (40 mg/kg), or melittin (80 mg/kg). All groups except the control received topical IMQ for seven days.

extracted_findings.effect: Reduces psoriatic inflammation via mTOR suppression and autophagy activation
